Q: How and when does ngen.exe work? A:

When a .NET compiler compiles C# or VB.NET code it half compiles them and creates CIL code. When you run this half-compiled .NET EXE file the JIT runs in the background and compiles the half-compiled CIL code in to full machine language. This mode is termed as normal JIT.

You can also go the other way around saying you do not want runtime compilation by running a full compiled EXE file. This compilation is done by using negen.exe. In this scenario the JIT does not participate at runtime. This is termed as pre-JIT mode.

If you want to see how they affect performance you can see this YouTube video which demonstrates normal-JIT and pre-JIT mode of compilation:

Q: Failing to check A:

The issue is likely not with the any() logic itself, but with how hybrid commands handle interactions and potential blocking operations in the database.

1. Interaction Timeout

In discord.py, a hybrid_command (Slash Command) requires a response within 3 seconds. If roles_db.insert_one is a synchronous operation (like standard PyMongo) and it takes a bit too long, the interaction will expire, and the code will simply stop executing without sending a message.

2. Solution: Defer and Check Types

You should defer the interaction to give your bot more time (up to 15 minutes) and ensure your IDs are being compared correctly.

@custom.command(name="register", description="Registers a custom role to a user")
async def register(self, ctx: commands.Context, role: discord.Role, member: discord.Member):
    # This gives the bot more time to process the DB insert
    await ctx.defer()

    # Ensure admin IDs are integers (role.id is always an int)
    user_role_ids = [r.id for r in ctx.author.roles]
    is_admin = any(role_id in admin for role_id in user_role_ids)

    if is_admin:
        # Note: if roles_db is synchronous, it blocks the event loop.
        # Consider using 'motor' for async MongoDB or run_in_executor.
        roles_db.insert_one({"user_id": member.id, "role_id": role.id})
        await ctx.send(f"✅ Role {role.name} registered for {member.display_name}!")
    else:
        await ctx.send("❌ You do not have the required role.")

3. Debugging steps

If it still doesn't work, verify the following:

  • Intents: Ensure intents.members is enabled in your bot setup and on the Discord Developer Portal. Without it, ctx.author.roles might only contain the @everyone role.

  • Data Types: Check your utils/variables.py. If the IDs in the admin list are strings (e.g., "14084..."), the comparison r.id in admin will always be False because r.id is an integer. They must be numbers without quotes.

Q: Secret in version "v1" cannot be handled as a Secret: v1.Secret.Data: ReadMapCB: expect { or n, but found ", error found in #10 byte of A:

When you paste the base64 password, it splits the password between a few lines and adds spaces in between the lines. It is difficult to explain and there is no need to add space after .dockerconfigjson, as the yaml provided in the tutorial is correct. The problem occurs after pasting the base64-encoded-json.

Open the secret in Vim and run: :set listchars+=space:␣ and then :set list this will show all the spaces as ␣, check if there is none between the password lines. This worked in my case.

Update: The Vim command does not always show the spaces, so just navigate to the begging of each line of your secret key and press backspace so they connect.

Q: mysql crashing with "mysqld got signal 11" A:

Considering these 2 posted lines of key_buffer information, | Key_blocks_unused | 857368 | | Key_blocks_used | 3 |

Suggestion for your my.cnf/ini [mysqld] section 

key_buffer_size=1M  # from 1G which is USED very little.

and to get max_threads to a reasonable number, this is the variable name

thread_cache_size=100  # from 2000 v5.7 5.1.5 CAP at 100

Q: How reduce background noise while recording in iphone? A:

There is a special kind software to remove background audio noises. Audacity for PC might be one of the most popular (it is open source by the way). Also, you could do that entirely on iPhone with the Denoise app.

Basically, recorded audio contains a lof of individual sounds and some of them are harmful (a.e. buzzing lamps, street noises, mic issues, etc.). A very popular approach to suppress harmful sounds is to calculate frequency spectre of harmful noises and supress "harmful" frequencies throughout the whole audio duration. In both, Audacity and Denoise you do that by selecting a "noise only" fragment. All sounds in that fragment are considered to be noises and are suppressed in whole file.

If you need to incorporate this feature into your app then you could have a look at the Audacity sources. Please let me know if you need more details.

Q: Bun in VS Code: error "Cannot find name Bun" when using the Bun singleton A:

For those who are still encountering this issue, here is the updated fix

  1. Install the @types/bun as the dev dependency
bun add -d @types/bun
  1. Update tsconfig.json compilerOptions > types (add if missing)
{
  "compilerOptions": {
     "types": ["bun"],
//..

Q: Objects destroyed too early in recursive structure using std::vector when using auto A:

In lines like:

auto alpha = root.add("alpha");

alpha is actually a copy because a reference is not inferred by default.
Therefore adding the sub nodes is not done with the intended node, but rather with a copy of it.

If you change it to:

//---v---------------------------
auto & alpha = root.add("alpha");

(and similarly change for beta and gamma),
You will get the expected result.

Live demo - Compiler explorer
